newsitem.title: CHINA: China state sector needs non-state treatment.
newsitem.headline: China state sector needs non-state treatment.

text.p: China's economic gurus should apply the same policies to the loss-making state sector as to the burgeoning and successful non-state sector, a prominent Chinese economist was quoted as saying in the Business News on Thursday.

The newspaper quoted Fan Gang as saying 80 percent of China's economic growth and 90 percent of new job opportunities could be attributed to the non-state sector, and that these proportions were growing.
But government policy favoured state-owned enterprises, he said, citing as an example the fact that state enterprises do not have to repay debts while private companies had no choice.
"The non-state sector has become the new source of China's economic growth and plays a more and more important role," Fan said.
"The government should implement an equal policy between the state and non-state sectors so that the new socialist market economy can gradually form and develop," he said.
Some 75 percent of China's 100,000 state-owned enterprises are in the red, with around 40 percent suffering chronic deficits, official figures show.
